info.title: API
info.description:
Platnova's Business API: collect payments with hosted checkout, issue virtual accounts and cards, send payouts, and receive webhooks.

# Authentication

Send your API key in the `X-API-Key` header on every request. Do not send it as `Authorization: Bearer`, and do not send a dashboard session token alongside it. The `api_key` query parameter is deprecated.

# Base URLs

- Live: https://api.platnova.com
- Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.platnova.co

# Errors

Most responses are `{status: boolean, data, error: [], message}`; branch on the HTTP status and `data.code`. Validation failures are HTTP 422 `{status: "error", message: "Validation failed", errors: {field: [messages]}}`. A missing or invalid key is 401 `un-authorized access`. See https://docs.platnova.com/errors.

post.description:
Open a virtual bank account for one of your customers.

**Name the customer** with `customer_id` or `customer_reference` (one of the two, not both). `customer_id` may be our customer id or your own id for the customer; `customer_reference` is your own id by its explicit name. If none of your customers has your id yet, send the customer's details (`customer_*` fields) and the customer is created with your id as their `reference`. A customer that already exists needs no details.

**Required for a new customer:** `customer_name` (or `customer_first_name` + `customer_last_name`), `customer_email`, `customer_phone`, `customer_country_code` (defaults to `NG` for NGN) and `customer_date_of_birth`. The date of birth is not needed for NGN when you send `id_number` (BVN): it is taken from the BVN record. `customer_gender` is optional.

**NGN:** in live, `id_number` (BVN) is required unless the customer already has a BVN on file, and it is verified before the account is opened.

**USD:** set a default USD settlement wallet in your dashboard; any account fee is charged to it. The customer needs an address and identity documents on file, so create USD customers with Create Customer first: a customer created from `customer_*` fields has neither.

**`reference`** (optional) opens an account for one loan or order. A customer can hold one account per reference, and repeating the request returns the same account. Without `reference`, a customer has one account per bank.

post.description: Initiate a payment transfer. Supports instant, scheduled, and recurring payments. Send your own unique `reference`: if the request times out, look the payment up by that reference with Verify Payment, and resend with the same reference only if it is not found. A reference is never paid twice.

transaction_ref.description: Platnova's unique reference for this payment. Verify Payment accepts it, and so does your own `reference`.

status.description: `pending` for a payout sent with an API key (it is on its way); `pending_approval` when a dashboard user without approval permission sent it. Follow it with Verify Payment or the `transfer.*` webhooks.

created_at.description: A readable time in your business's time zone, e.g. `Tuesday, 3 November, 09:15`. Not machine-readable: use `created_at` from Verify Payment.

400.description: Refused; nothing was sent (for example insufficient funds, or an invalid payload). A `reference` already used answers `data.code` `duplicate_reference` with the existing payment's `transaction_ref`. `data.code` `duplicate_payment`: the same amount to the same recipient less than a minute ago, sent with no `reference` and no `Idempotency-Key`. `idempotency_key_invalid` / `idempotency_key_required`: see Errors.

value.message: duplicate transaction detected: reference already exists

422.description: Validation error (e.g. invalid info fields for payment method) Also `data.code` `idempotency_key_reused`: the key was already used for a different request.

post.description: Check a payment by any of: the `transaction_ref` Send Payment returned, the `reference` you sent to Send Payment, a checkout id, the reference from a `checkout.paid` webhook, your order `reference` on a one-time virtual account, or the `transaction_ref` of an `account.funded` webhook. Only your own business's payments are found. Only `status` `success` means paid. 400 `payment_not_found` means no such payment exists for your business: for a payout, it was never created, so it is safe to resend with the same `reference`.

value.message: operation was successful

400.description: No payment with this reference for your business (`data.code` `payment_not_found`), or one of your checkouts not paid yet (`data.code` `checkout_unpaid`, `data.status` `pending` or `expired`). Any other 400 (for example `something went wrong, please contact support`) is not "not found": verify again.

DocumentInput.description: Identity document fields. Supported id_type values: passport, resident_id, drivers_license, national_id, voters_card, nin, bvn. For passport, resident_id, drivers_license, national_id, voters_card, and nin, provide at most front_doc as a base64-encoded image; back_doc is not required. These rules apply to each item in documents, to legacy document and additional_documents on create, and to each item in documents on update.

reference.description: Your own id for this customer. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, and `_ . : -`. Unique within your business. Once set, you can use it anywhere a customer id is accepted.

document.description: Legacy single primary identity document. Same shape and id_type values as each item in documents. Prefer documents when starting new integrations.

additional_documents.description: Legacy extra identity documents. Same id_type options and front/back rules as documents. The API merges these with documents server-side; prefer a single documents array when possible.

customer_id.description: Required unless you send `customer_reference`. Our customer id, or your own id for the customer. We look it up within your business: our id first, then a customer whose `reference` is this value. If neither matches and the request carries the customer's details (`customer_*` fields), the customer is created with this value as their `reference` (1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, and `_ . : -`). Without details, an unknown id answers `400` `customer was not found`.

customer_reference.description: Required unless you send `customer_id`. Your own id for the customer, by its explicit name. Works the same way as your id in `customer_id`, including creating a new customer from the `customer_*` fields. Send this or `customer_id`, not both.

id_number.description: The customer's BVN, for NGN accounts. In live it is required unless the customer already has a BVN on file, and it is verified before the account is opened. When sent for a new customer, `customer_date_of_birth` is not needed: it is taken from the BVN record.

reference.description: Optional. Your own reference for this account (a loan, an order). 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, and `_ . : -`. Unique among your business's accounts. A customer can hold one account per reference; repeating the request with the same reference, customer and currency returns the same account. Reusing it for another customer or currency answers `400` `duplicate_reference`.

codes.description: NGN: the issuing bank codes to open the account with (for example `100033`). Omit to use the first bank available to your business.

customer_name.description: New customer: full name, split at the first space into first and last name. Required unless you send `customer_first_name` and `customer_last_name`.

customer_first_name.description: New customer: first name. Send with `customer_last_name`, or send `customer_name` instead.

customer_last_name.description: New customer: last name. Send with `customer_first_name`, or send `customer_name` instead.

customer_email.description: New customer: required. A valid email address, unique among your customers.

customer_country_code.description: New customer: two-letter ISO country code. Defaults to `NG` for NGN; required otherwise.

customer_date_of_birth.description: New customer: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required, except for NGN when you send `id_number` (BVN): the date of birth is then taken from the BVN record.

CreateUserVirtualAccountRequest.description: Name the customer with `customer_id` or `customer_reference` (exactly one is required). The `customer_*` fields are read only when the customer does not exist yet.

customer_id.description: Required unless you send `customer_reference`. Our customer id, or your own id for the customer. We look it up within your business: our id first, then a customer whose `reference` is this value. If neither matches and the request carries the customer's details (`customer_*` fields), the customer is created with this value as their `reference` (1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, and `_ . : -`). Without details, an unknown id answers `400` `customer was not found`.

amount.description: The amount to collect (NGN). Payments of another amount are still credited; compare `expected_amount` and `paid_amount` on `account.funded`.

lifespan_minutes.description: How long the account stays open, in minutes (5 to 1440).

reference.description: Your own reference for the order this account collects. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, and `_ . : -`. Unique among your business's one-time accounts. Returned as `order_reference` and sent as `reference` on `account.funded`.

order_reference.description: Same as `reference`. Send one of them.

customer_reference.description: Required unless you send `customer_id`. Your own id for the customer, by its explicit name. Works the same way as your id in `customer_id`, including creating a new customer from the `customer_*` fields. Send this or `customer_id`, not both.

customer_name.description: New customer: full name, split at the first space into first and last name. Required unless you send `customer_first_name` and `customer_last_name`.

customer_first_name.description: New customer: first name. Send with `customer_last_name`, or send `customer_name` instead.

customer_last_name.description: New customer: last name. Send with `customer_first_name`, or send `customer_name` instead.

customer_email.description: New customer: required. A valid email address, unique among your customers.

customer_country_code.description: New customer: two-letter ISO country code. Defaults to `NG`.

CreateDynamicVirtualAccountRequest.description: Name the customer with `customer_id` or `customer_reference` (exactly one is required). The `customer_*` fields are read only when the customer does not exist yet.

wallet_id.description: Wallet ID for the account currency

customer_id.description: Our customer id, or your own `reference` for the customer.

payment_method.description: One of: card, bank_transfer, mobile_money, wallet, tag_transfer, defi, revolut, paypal, cashapp, zelle, ussd

info.description: Recipient details; required fields depend on payment_method (e.g. account_number, bank_code, account_name for bank_transfer; tag_id for tag_transfer)

reference.description: Your own unique id for this payment. A reference can be used once per business: resending one already used is refused with `data.code` `duplicate_reference` and nothing is sent. Use it to look the payment up with Verify Payment if the send times out.

frequency.description: For recurring: e.g. daily, weekly, monthly

approver.description: Account UID to notify for approval (non-owner)

reference.description: Any of: the `transaction_ref` returned by Send Payment, the `reference` you sent to Send Payment, a checkout id, the reference from a `checkout.paid` webhook, the `reference` you gave a one-time account for an order, or the `transaction_ref` of an `account.funded` webhook.

amount.description: Fixed amount; required when customer.can_set_price is false

can_set_price.description: If true, payer can choose amount; then amount may be omitted

limit.description: Max number of payments per link

email.description: Email of the user (customer) in the entity to invoice

reference.description: Your reference, unique across your business.

customer_name.description: The name the biller holds for the account.

amount.description: NGN credited to the customer's betting wallet.

fee.description: NGN charged to you on top of amount.

unit_amount.description: More than 0, at most two decimals.

amount.description: Major units (naira, dollars). At most two decimals.

currency.description: Lowercase wallet currency, e.g. ngn, usd, gbp, eur, kes, ghs.

partner_reference.description: Your order id. Echoed on GET checkout and in checkout.paid.

line_items.description: quantity × unit_amount over all lines must equal amount.

payment_options.description: Ignored: every live method is offered.

source.description: `api` for a sale made with an API key; `platform` for a dashboard self top-up.

purpose.description: `self_deposit` for a self top-up; absent for a sale.

id.description: Internal record id. You don't need it.

ref.description: Platnova's unique reference for the payment. For a payout, the `transaction_ref` Send Payment returned. Quote it to support.

reference.description: Payouts: the `reference` you sent to Send Payment. Customer payments into virtual accounts: your order's or account's reference. Empty if none, and for checkout payments.

amount.description: What you were credited (checkout) or sent (payout).

paid_amount.description: Checkout and customer payments: what the payer sent.

status.description: Only `success` means paid. `success`: paid, final. `failed`, `cancelled`, `reversed`: not paid, final; the money is back in your wallet. `pending`, `processing`, `pending_approval`, `under_review`: not final yet; check again later or wait for the webhook. Treat any value other than `success` as not paid. For a payout: a failed payout reads `cancelled` (amount and fee returned), and so does one reversed after it succeeded (amount returned, fee kept); `failed` is only a scheduled payout that found too little in the wallet when it was due, and nothing was debited.

customer_id.description: Customer payments into virtual accounts: our customer id.

customer_reference.description: Customer payments: your own id for the customer, when set.

expected_amount.description: Order payments: the amount the order's account was opened for. Compare with `paid_amount`.

amount.description: Omit for the full refundable amount.

state.description: `answered`: the request finished; the same key and body return the same answer. `in_progress`: it may still be running; ask again shortly. `no_answer`: it stopped without an answer (our error, or a crash). The key will never run again.

nothing_created.description: `true` only when the request can no longer create anything and created nothing: you may send the payment again **under a new key**. `false` with `payment` null means we can't be sure yet; ask again later rather than paying twice.

payment.description: What the request created, or null.

type.description: `transaction` for a payout or conversion; `recurring_payment`; card routes answer `card`, `customer_card` or `customer_transaction`.

ref.description: For a payout, the `transaction_ref` Send Payment would have answered.

id.description: Platnova's id for the customer: the `customer_id` the other customer routes take.

reference.description: Your own id for the customer; `null` if you set none.

id.description: The wallet's id: what Send Payment takes as `from_wallet_id`. A plain UUID, with no prefix.

amount.description: The balance, as a decimal string.

label.description: A name you gave the wallet; may be empty.

is_default.description: Whether this is a default wallet.

BankStatus.description: How transfers to one bank are going right now. Show `message` to your customer as it is; it never names a payment provider. A warning never blocks a payout: you decide whether to send.

level.description: green: transfers arrive as usual. amber: slow right now. red: having problems; a transfer may be delayed. grey: no recent transfer data.

message.example: Zenith Bank is slow right now. Transfers are taking about 8 minutes.

expected_minutes.description: Typical arrival time in minutes; null for red and grey

as_of.description: When this status was computed; null when we hold no data for the bank

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid API key (`un-authorized access`).

NotActive.description: The business is not live: `data.code` = `entity_not_active`, `data.missing` lists what is left.

Conflict.description: A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running (`request_in_progress`). Retry after Retry-After.

Validation.description: Validation failed, or Idempotency-Key reused for a different request.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed per minute on this route

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: the same key and body replays the first answer.
